image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a single white daisy flower with a bright yellow center. A small insect (appearing to be a fly or bee) is perched on the upper part of the yellow disc. The background is a soft, out-of-focus green, suggesting foliage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Composite flower with central yellow disc surrounded by single whorl of white ray petals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows a composite structure with a distinct yellow center and radiating white petals.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flower head is modest in size with numerous elongated white petals radiating outward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Petals are elongated and radiate correctly from the center; count appears consistent with species norms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright yellow center with bumpy, granular texture from individual disc florets.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The yellow disc exhibits high-frequency texture consistent with disc florets, not a smooth plastic surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Petals narrow, slightly pointed, arranged in flat, circular pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Petal morphology matches the description; they are narrow with rounded-to-pointed tips and lie relatively flat.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Slender green stem supporting flower head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight macro shot focused on the flower head; the stem is completely occluded or outside the frame.
No stem or leaves are visible in the frame due to the close-up cropping.
Ground and stem base are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Single stem supporting composite flower head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Cannot verify stem structure as it is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Central disc florets form textured yellow center.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Redundant with Flower_or_Top checkpoint but visually confirmed; texture is present.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that the subject is indeed a daisy and not a look-alike (e.g., chamomile) or AI-hallucinated hybrid.
To detect subtle texture anomalies in the petals and center, such as melting, smearing, or inconsistent lighting.
To ensure individual petals are distinct entities without fusion at the base or bleeding into the background.
To identify the secondary subject (insect) and ensure it doesn't introduce structural artifacts or fusion with the flower.

focus_areas: Texture consistency of the yellow disc florets
Boundary sharpness between white petals and green background
Structural integrity of the insect on the flower
Symmetry and natural variation of petal arrangement
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the junction where the white petals meet the yellow center. AI generators often blur this boundary or create a 'halo' effect. Also, verify if the insect's legs interact physically with the flower surface or if they appear to float/fuse.
